solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Source of lies that hurts a clergyman's office in a sinister way

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: a cry of pain, the exclamation ouch
Ely is a bishop's see, the seat of his office

explanation.surface: Someone fibbing about a wounded vicar's workplace, doing it in a shady manner.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's office or jurisdiction, and Ely is the crossword's favourite see.
explanation.definitionFit: Louche means disreputable or shady, so the adverb describes acting in a dubious, sinister fashion.

clue.text: Attack allowed to pass quickly

parts.note: let means allowed
time flies, it passes quickly

explanation.surface: An assault that was permitted to go by fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To let fly is an idiom for launching an attack, verbal or physical.

clue.text: As one promoter of peace oversees hostility, nothing must interrupt

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, works to promote peace

indicators.note: the zero breaks into the middle of the word

parts.note: animus is hostility or ill will
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: A united peacekeeping body monitors a conflict that must not be paused.
explanation.definitionFit: Unanimous means everyone agrees, acting together with one voice.

clue.text: Back-to-back houses are causing a fuss

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house

indicators.note: two copies placed back to back, the second turned round to face the first

parts.note: HO is an abbreviation for house
an are is a metric unit of area, A

explanation.surface: Terraced housing is stirring up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-to-back houses are British terraced homes sharing a rear wall; here HO and OH meet back to back.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoo-ha is an informal word for a commotion or row, a to-do.

clue.text: Supply plant with article to be packaged

indicators.note: the article is packaged inside the flower's name

parts.note: a lily is a flowering plant
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Delivering a flower with a newspaper piece in a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the verb: it is the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply, from supple, means in a flexible, lissom way, as one moves nimbly.

clue.text: Supposedly diet-enhancing drug causes a scene

parts.note: lo-cal food is low in calories, supposedly helping a diet
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A slimming pill turns out to cause a public fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: LO-CAL is the advertising spelling of low-calorie; 'causes' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A locale is the place where something happens, its setting or scene.

clue.text: Run from public dispute about hospital

indicators.note: the dispute is about, concerning, the hospital, which comes first

parts.note: overt means open or public
a row is a dispute or quarrel

explanation.surface: Fleeing an open quarrel over a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is a cricket run, not fleeing; 'from' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an overthrow is a stray return that lets the batsmen take an extra run.

clue.text: A region that's short of space

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: a realm is a region or domain

explanation.surface: An area that lacks room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of space' looks like the deletion; 'short' does that alone and 'of space' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Areal means relating to area, the extent of a space or surface.

clue.text: Seduced yours truly turning up on set

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above
in a down answer the word turns upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: the setter, me
bedded means took to bed, seduced

explanation.surface: I was seduced, arriving on a film set.
explanation.definitionFit: Embedded means fixed firmly in surrounding matter, set in place.

clue.text: Agency rejected something a little shocking by adult actor

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: art in its old sense of means or agency, as in 'by art'
a volt is a unit of electrical potential, a small shock
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A talent agency turns down a mildly scandalous offer from a grown-up performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ART to TRA; 'a little shocking' is electrical, not scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: John Travolta is a Hollywood film star, an example of an actor.

clue.text: Echo note right back

indicators.note: sent back, so the two pieces are read in reverse order and letter

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: An instruction to send a reply straight back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns BREVER into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is an echoing effect added to sound.

clue.text: Bird's limited visibility when flying north

indicators.note: in a down answer, flying north means reading upwards, backwards
only a limited stretch of the word's letters is used

explanation.surface: A bird can see little when heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' takes SIBI from visibility; 'when flying north' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: Galileo endlessly moved her

indicators.note: the remaining letters are moved about into a new order
without its ends, so the first and last letters of the name are dropped

explanation.surface: The astronomer's discoveries stirred a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves ALILE, which 'moved' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Leila is a female forename, so the pronoun stands for a woman bearing it.

clue.text: Involved in conflict, he arranged for Wombles to interrupt section of teledrama

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the middle of the other

parts.note: a section, or run of letters, from the middle of the word teledrama
Mike Batt arranged and wrote the Wombles' music, giving M. BATT

explanation.surface: A man scoring a children's TV show cuts into a drama in the middle of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are furry characters from a British children's TV show and pop group, whose songs Mike Batt arranged and wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Embattled describes someone beset by fighting or difficulty, caught up in conflict.

clue.text: Warm to a place of debauchery

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, figuratively a place of filth and debauchery

explanation.surface: Getting heated on the way to a den of vice.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal word for pleasantly warm, like toast.

clue.text: One could be caught at sea if clashes get stormy

definitions.text: One could be caught at sea

indicators.note: letters that get stormy are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: Seafarers' quarrels could become violent out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalefish is a bony fish with scales, as opposed to shellfish, the kind trawlers catch.

clue.text: Safe to hold odd bits of brass moulding

indicators.note: one word holds the other, so the picked letters sit inside it

parts.note: sure in the sense of secure or safe

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A strongbox containing scattered brass fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' brass gives B, A, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A surbase is a moulding or border running along the top of a skirting or pedestal.

clue.text: Jet wash

definitions.meaning: a jet is a stream of air or gas
the wash of an aircraft is the disturbed air behind it

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like 'jet-wash', cleaning with a hose; each is a flow of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A current of moving air is both a jet and the wash left by an aircraft.

clue.text: Loose snow that's thawed around dry bit of ice

indicators.note: the slush goes around the other pieces

parts.note: slush is half-melted snow
TT, teetotal, is dry

indicators.note: a bit of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Melting snow around a dry patch of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' in the old sense of immoral; TT (teetotal) is the crossword's dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluttish once meant slovenly or morally lax, which is loose in the old censorious sense.

clue.text: Run away from sailor left by a noted venue?

indicators.note: the letter goes away from the word, so it is removed

parts.note: a lascar is an East Indian sailor
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fleeing a seaman who was abandoned by a woman at a famous place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' means full of musical notes: the venue is an opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is the world's best-known opera house, a venue for notes.

clue.text: Nadal returned from baseline to baseline?

indicators.note: sent back like a tennis return, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Rafa is the familiar name of tennis player Rafael Nadal

explanation.surface: The Spanish star returns a ball the full length of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: The two baselines are the far ends of a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great distance, as one baseline is from the other.

clue.text: Alter banger, perhaps after Formula One quits

indicators.note: the abbreviation quits the word, so its letters are removed

parts.note: a banger is a loud firework (in Britain also a sausage)
Formula One is F1, written FI

explanation.surface: Modifying a car, perhaps once it leaves motor racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' suggests an old car beside Formula One; here it is a noisy firework.
explanation.definitionFit: To rework something is to revise or remake it, which alters it.

clue.text: Agony aunt regularly treated injury

indicators.note: taking every other letter, at regular intervals

parts.note: a burn is an injury

explanation.surface: A problem-page writer routinely dealt with a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks R, A, E from treated.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Raeburn is a British advice columnist and broadcaster, an example of a problem-page writer.

clue.text: Most retiring professors essentially in trouble?

indicators.note: the middle letters go inside the word for trouble

parts.note: to be in the shit is slang for being in trouble

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: Are the shyest academics really in difficulty?
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' picks ES, the centre of professors.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiest is a variant superlative of shy, the most bashful or retiring.

clue.text: Invite requires a long time in European continent

indicators.note: the outer word requires the period to be placed within it
signals that the long time goes inside the invitation word

parts.note: to tempt is to invite or entice
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An invitation needs a long stay on mainland Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continent' looks like Europe, but it is the adjective meaning self-restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent as an adjective means exercising self-restraint, which is moderate or temperate.

clue.text: Misogamist twice visited place associated with vice?

indicators.note: only two short stops are made in the word, so the letters between and after them are skipped

explanation.surface: A hater of marriage went somewhere twice, a place of sin?
explanation.walkthrough: The two visits take MI and AMI from misogamist. Miami Vice was a TV cop show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida city gave its name to the TV police drama Miami Vice.

clue.text: Time in hide curtailed — out with it!

indicators.note: the time abbreviation goes inside the shortened word
cut short at the tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cache is a hiding place, a hide

explanation.surface: An impatient demand to hear what's hidden, cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a catch dismisses a batsman: with it, he is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a catch gets the batsman out, so the ball caught brings dismissal.

clue.text: Old hunt expert going after champion

indicators.note: the expert piece goes after, below, the champion

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A master pursues the winner in a traditional chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Chace is an obsolete spelling of chase, a hunt.

clue.text: East wing of infirmary about to admit one from Rome?

indicators.note: the pieces let a letter in between them
the east, right-hand end of the word is kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: an infirmary is a hospital
C is short for circa, about
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hospital wing is about to take in a patient from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East wing' is the right-hand part, ITAL, of hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic means relating to ancient Italy, so it describes things Roman in origin, as italic type is.

clue.text: African petition about Europeans

indicators.note: the first word goes about, around, the second

parts.note: to sue is to petition or appeal
Danes are people from Denmark, Europeans

explanation.surface: An African's plea concerning people from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sudanese person comes from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Measurement of a letter by its position in the alphabet

parts.note: the letter H
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Reads like a typographer's way of measuring letters by their order.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is H, and its place in the alphabet is eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Height is a dimension, how tall something is, a kind of measurement.

clue.text: Merit in working before start of tea break

indicators.note: working on letters reshapes them into a new order
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A worker's merit before the tea break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges MERITIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to suspend or interrupt for a while, to break off.
